body_markdown:
Agreement makes CVSR’s inverters available to support transmission voltage stability around the clock, extending solar’s reliability value beyond daylight hours


SAN FRANCISCO — Clearway Energy Group (“Clearway”) announced today that its California Valley Solar Ranch (“CVSR”), a 250-megawatt solar facility in San Luis Obispo County, California, has entered into an agreement with Pacific Gas and Electric Company (“PG&E”) to provide dispatchable reactive power support to PG&E’s transmission network during nighttime hours.


Under the agreement, CVSR’s inverters remain energized after sunset and, when dispatched by PG&E, inject or absorb reactive power to help maintain voltage stability on the local transmission network. The inverters are used to support grid voltage independent of solar production.


“This agreement is a good example of what our existing fleet is capable of beyond generating power during daylight hours,” said Drew Worts, Vice President of Operations at Clearway. “CVSR’s inverters were already providing voltage support during the day, and now we’re putting that capability to work for the grid around the clock. It’s a meaningful step in how we expand the reliability value of our solar assets.”


“This is a great example of how we can unlock hidden value in resources already connected to the grid,” said Brian Soest, supervisor, Grid Operations at PG&E. “By working with Clearway to use existing solar inverters in a new way, we can support grid reliability while creating additional value from clean energy infrastructure even when the sun isn’t shining.”


This agreement establishes one of the first examples in California for solar generating facilities to provide grid-support services outside their hours of energy production, effectively making solar assets available as a 24/7 reliability resource rather than a daylight-only generation source.


CVSR has delivered solar power to PG&E under long-term power purchase agreements since 2013 and remains one of the largest operating solar photovoltaic facilities in the county.
